summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 48% to INR304.41 crore and PAT 64% to INR22.2 crore (7.59% margin); Melt N Mellow hit 7% EBITDA ahead of plan.
summary.overview: Krishival Foods reported FY26 revenue of INR304.41 crore (up 48% YoY), EBITDA of INR41.95 crore (margin 13.78%, up 66%) and PAT of INR22.2 crore (margin 7.59%, up 89 bps). The ice cream arm Melt N Mellow reached about 7% EBITDA on roughly INR95 crore of revenue, a year ahead of its FY27 plan. Management guided FY27 to about 50% top-line growth and 50%+ bottom-line growth. Q4 EBITDA margin looked weaker on a reported basis, which management attributed to seasonal nuts B2B pressure and a INR2.88 crore ESOP charge booked in ice cream; it said the adjusted Q4 margin was 12.21% vs 12.03% in Q4 FY25.

segments.name: Krishival Nuts & Dry Fruits
segments.commentary: Nuts revenue grew from about INR50 crore (Mar 2022) to INR173 crore in FY26 per management; FY26 EBITDA margin about 15% and PAT margin about 10%. Existing plant ran at about 70% utilisation in FY26.

segments.name: Melt N Mellow (Ice cream)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR95 crore in FY26 with about 7% EBITDA; ice cream sales were about INR47 crore in the first nine months and about INR43 crore in Q4. Existing capacity of 1 lakh litres per day ran at about 25% utilisation in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27: about 50% top-line growth and 50%+ bottom-line growth (company-level).
Nuts: maintain about 15%+ EBITDA and 10%+ PAT in the next two years; PAT to stay above 10% even as depreciation rises.
Ice cream: EBITDA to stay above 7% and rise; target 14-15% EBITDA about three years out once capacity is fully used; FY27 PAT above 3% (stated conservatively).
Ice cream capacity: full utilisation targeted by Q1 FY29.
About 25 company-operated, franchise-owned Mellow & Co. parlours to open in Pune and Mumbai, starting July-August 2026; management expects each to break even from month three.
Ice cream share of total sales to keep rising in FY27; management expects nuts and ice cream to be roughly equal by FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: Nuts capacity raised from 10 to 20 metric tons per day of finished product; the new 35,000 sq ft unit began production in April 2026. Plan is 30 MT/day next year and 40 MT/day after that, within a 2 lakh sq ft Halkarni MIDC factory under construction.

Nuts utilisation: existing 10 MT/day capacity expected near 90% in FY27; new 10 MT/day capacity expected about 25% utilised in FY27, with a further 25-50% of the enhanced capacity to be used the year after.
Ice cream: deep freezer network expanded from about 3,000 to over 15,000 in FY26 and will keep growing in FY27.
Ice cream capacity of 1 lakh litres per day; utilisation about 25% in FY26.
demand_pricing: Melt N Mellow footprint: 34,200 retail outlets (up from about 25,000 at acquisition, per management's comment that it had 37,000 retail touchpoints later in the call), 189+ ice cream SKUs.
Nuts: 11,000 retail touchpoints, 67+ SKUs; Krishival present in 300+ Indian towns and 300+ retail points in Singapore.
FY26 volumes: about 4.74 crore Magic Cones, 3.5 crore Chocobars and 1.78 crore cups and sundaes sold.
Ice cream demand: more than 50% from Maharashtra; Andhra Pradesh launched November 2025 and Bengaluru around October-November 2025, both said to be picking up.

Management said nuts pricing power comes from Tier 2-4 distribution and in-house sourcing; it sees competition from large FMCG players (e.g., Tata Consumer) as a sign of a growing category, and said sourcing depth is a barrier for them.
Management described near-term input cost volatility for imported commodities but said it sees no structural impact on growth.

qa_highlights.question: When will the expanded nuts capacity reach peak utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nuts capacity is 20 MT/day now (from 10), with 25% utilisation of the new capacity in FY27 and the existing unit near 90%, and further steps to 30 and 40 MT/day over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT margins for nuts at steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15%+ EBITDA and 10%+ PAT for the next two years, with EBITDA possibly rising a couple of points but PAT held at 10%+ despite higher depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is seasonally weak for nuts (B2B wedding demand) and that a INR2.88 crore ESOP charge sat in ice cream; excluding it, Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 12.21% vs 12.03% in Q4 FY25. Management said FY27 ESOP cost would be below the FY26 level.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the consolidated raw material cost increase in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher ice cream volumes in Q4, which need more raw material and packaging (RMPM), with ice cream sales of about INR43 crore in Q4 versus about INR47 crore in the first nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Where is ice cream demand coming from and how will sales promotion costs evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is over 50% from Maharashtra, with Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Andhra Pradesh the other focus states; management said branding spend will be set as a percentage of sales and funded from rising EBITDA, with no sharp unplanned jump.

qa_highlights.question: How were IPO, preferential and rights issue funds deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: IPO proceeds of about INR20 crore and a preferential issue of about INR65 crore went into nuts working capital. Of the INR100 crore rights issue, INR35 crore was received in January 2026 (INR25 crore for Halkarni plant and machinery, INR10 crore for nuts working capital); the remaining INR65 crore is due in two calls in calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What synergy did the company get from acquiring Melt N Mellow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the existing milk and raw material sourcing, the distributor network, complementary working-capital cycles against nuts, and founders' R&D depth; it said the ice cream retail network can be used to sell nuts over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the preferential allottees' shareholding and related inquiry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had no comment on the matter and that the investors were shareholders; it said it had no involvement in any wrongdoing by investors who are not part of management.

risks_watch: Ice cream Q4 margin optics and ESOP costs, with FY27 ESOP to be below the INR2.88 crore charge booked in Q4 FY26.
Execution risk on 25 Mellow & Co. company-operated parlours from July-August 2026, which add overhead and capex.
Input cost volatility for globally sourced commodities and rising RM/PM needs as ice cream volume grows.
Nuts utilisation ramp for the new 10 MT/day capacity (25% assumed in FY27) and depreciation impact on PAT.
Pending INR65 crore rights-issue calls due in 2026.
Competitive entry in nuts by large FMCG players.
Questions on preferential allottees' shareholding were answered without detail, so this remains an open governance point.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 growth and ice cream profitability, with a heavy focus on phased, self-funded expansion. Evasive on specifics: the answers on the preferential allottees and some segment-margin questions were brief, and the ESOP and Q4 margin explanations were repetitive.
key_quotes: What differentiates us is clear , we are building scale with profitability, not at the cost of it.
This year, 7% EBITDA on a top line of INR 95 crores has been achieved, which is ahead of our planned profitability which was planned in FY '27.
So EBITDA will not go below 7%. It will keep on increasing.
